2 PROJECT DETAILS
2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability
2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB,
G1.2)
The Lisala REDD+ Project (hereinafter “the Project”) is a REDD+ initiative that aims to implement an
integrated and comprehensive approach designed to reduce carbon emissions by addressing the drivers
of deforestation and forest degradation in the DRC, namely slash-and-burn agriculture and charcoal
production. The overall objective of the Lisala REDD+ Project is to draw inspiration from the approaches of
the PIREDD Mai-Ndombe (supported by the Forest Investment Program (FIP) and the Central African Forest
Initiative (CAFI) with the World Bank as the executing agency), to improve community livelihoods and forest
landscape management, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and forest
degradation in the concession.
The activities of the Lisala REDD+ Project will be implemented within the conservation concession No.
04/24 (hereinafter “the concession”), located in the Lisala territory of the province of Mongala, in the
Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The Project zone encompasses the entire surface of the concession,
covering an area of 182’751 hectares, primarily covered by forests (148’642 hectares) and rural
development areas (34’109 hectares). The forests in the concession that were previously intended for
logging have been converted to conservation areas.
Situated in the heart of the Congo Basin forests, the concession comprises approximately 63 villages with
a growing population of around 72k people, mainly located along its outer boundaries. Human activities in
the region, particularly agriculture, are causing deforestation that is progressing towards the heart of the
concession.
- The Lisala REDD+ project aims to combat deforestation by identifying its various drivers and
working closely with local authorities as well as all relevant stakeholders. To this end, it will
implement a coherent and coordinated territorial approach, drawing on the different pillars of the
Democratic Republic of Congo’s National REDD+ Strategy. The project’s operational framework
includes the following strategic action areas:
- Local authorities with enhanced powers will organize land use planning exercises within village
communities;
- Trained and motivated technical extension services will monitor and support community forest
management;
- Support will be provided for the development of management plans that are adapted to the region's
agricultural environment;
- Training and supervision of small-scale foresters will be provided, alongside the dissemination of
agricultural techniques to increase yields and incomes for the rural population;
- Family planning initiatives will be considered to manage population growth over the medium term;
- Rehabilitation of public infrastructure (school and health center) will be supported through Local
Development Funds.
As described above, the project's activities aim to achieve ambitious goals in restoring and preserving
biodiversity, strengthening communities' capacity for action and supporting their economic development,
as well as promoting climate change mitigation. This will result in reduced pressure on forests, which will
lead to a reduction in unplanned deforestation and the restoration of forest ecosystems, the development

Page 6
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
6
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
of sustainable and profitable agricultural activities for communities, the establishment of a system that
integrates the various communities in an inclusive and participatory manner in the management of
concession resources, and the rehabilitation of public infrastructure (schools, health centers, roads, and
water sources) that will reduce poverty and the isolation of villages.
The project is aligned with the national REDD+ strategy, established in 2012, which aims to stabilize forest
cover at 63.5% by 2030. It fully complies with all applicable DRC legislation for REDD+ project development,
including submission to the national REDD+ approval process, the securing of Free, Prior and Informed
Consent (FPIC) from local communities, and the completion of a social and environmental impact
assessment.
The Project applies the VCS approved VM0007 (v.1.8) Methodology Framework and is expected to reduce
emissions by an average of 719 149 tCO2/year, and a total of 21’5 million tCO2 during the first crediting
period of 30 years.
The Project is not located within a jurisdiction covered by a jurisdictional REDD+ program.

2.1.4 Project Eligibility (VCS, 3.1, 3.6, 3.8, 3.18, 4.1; CCB Program Rules, 4.2.4, 4.6.4)
The Lisala REDD+ Project is eligible to participate under both the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Program
and the Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) Standards, as demonstrated below.
Under the VCS Program, the project complies with all applicable program rules, including legal compliance,
use of eligible and approved methodologies, and adherence to the latest version of the standard (currently
v4.7). The project respects national laws, regulations, and customary rights in accordance with Congolese
legislation, as further detailed in Section 2.5.1.
The project applies the VCS-approved VM0007 REDD+ Methodology Framework (REDD-MF), version 1.8,
which is currently eligible and active under the VCS Program. All relevant modules and tools required by
this methodology, including the AFOLU Non-Permanence Risk Tool and modules for baseline determination
and leakage accounting, will be implemented. The project uses standardized approaches for demonstrating
additionality and establishing baselines, and applies all default parameters and factors in full compliance
with the VCS Methodology Requirements.
The Lisala REDD+ Project falls under VCS Scope 14 (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use) and is
classified as an Avoided Unplanned Deforestation (AUD) activity. It aims to reduce GHG emissions primarily
associated with slash-and-burn agriculture and unsustainable wood extraction within the Lisala
conservation concession in Mongala Province. The project area encompasses approximately 148 642
hectares of natural forests. It is designed as a single-location project and does not incorporate grouped
that would involve adding new activity instances after validation.
The project start date is 1 March 2025. It will be listed on the Verra Registry within the same year, and
validation will occur within the five-year timeframe required for large-scale AFOLU projects under the VCS
Program. Prior to validation, the project will complete the required 30-day public comment period, and the
validation report and statement will be submitted within one year following the close of this period, in
compliance with VCS requirements.
The Lisala REDD+ Project is also eligible under the CCB Standards. It delivers significant benefits for
climate, communities, and biodiversity. Beyond reduce emissions by avoiding deforestation, the project
also supports sustainable development through participatory land-use planning, sustainable agricultural
practices, and investments in infrastructure such as schools and health centers, contributing to improved
livelihoods and social welfare for local communities. In terms of biodiversity, the project intend to preserves
148 642 hectares of tropical forest within the Congo Basin, recognized as one of the world’s most critical
biodiversity hotspots.
Stakeholder engagement was conducted through inclusive, culturally appropriate consultations led by the
Congolese NGO AMAR, ensuring that Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) was obtained from all
relevant communities. A grievance redress mechanism is in place to manage potential conflicts and ensure
ongoing dialogue with stakeholders.

CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
Legal rights over the concession are secured through a formal contract between Equaforest SARLU (now
Taranis Congo) and the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo. Taranis Operations Limited, as
the project proponent, is undergoing the REDD+ investment homologation process required under
Ministerial Order No. 047/CAB/MIN/EDD/AAN/MMUOS/2018, which, once completed, will secure
exclusive rights over the Emission Reductions generated by the project.
The project does not conflict with any existing VCS or other GHG program rules and all validation and
verification activities will be conducted in accordance with ISO 14064-3 and ISO 17029, ensuring
compliance with the VCS Program requirements for third-party validation and verification.

2.1.9 Project Ownership (VCS, 3.2, 3.7, 3.10; CCB, G5.8)
Land Ownership
The concession rights to the conservation concession No. 04/24 have been granted to Equaforest, later
renamed Taranis Congo, subsidiary of Taranis Operations Limited (Project Proponent), pursuant to the
signing of a conservation concession agreement on December 5, 2024, between the Democratic
Republic of Congo, represented by the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development and
Equaforest (now Taranis Congo), for a duration of 25 years.
Project Ownership
The Lisala REDD+ Project is led by Taranis Operations Limited, acting as the Project Proponent. In
accordance with Article 3 of Ministerial Decree No. 047/CAB/MIN/EDD/AAN/MMUOS/2018 of May 9,
2018 2, which defines the procedure for approving REDD+ investments in the Democratic Republic of
Congo, the State has exclusive ownership rights over Congolese Emission Reductions Units (ERUs) and
may transfer them to the REDD+ investment holder, if and only if the latter validates the legal
homologation procedure imposed by Article 3 of Ministerial Decree No.
047/CAB/MIN/EDD/AAN/MMUOS/2018 of May 9, 2018.
An irrevocable and enforceable collaboration agreement between Taranis Congo, acting on behalf of
Taranis Operations Limited, and the Democratic Republic of Congo represented by the Ministry of
Environment and Sustainable Development has been signed. This agreement sets out the terms and
conditions of cooperation between the Parties and their respective rights and obligations in connection
with the implementation of the Project. This agreement confirms the government's approval of the Project
and acknowledges Taranis Operations Limited's exclusive ownership rights over the carbon credits
generated by the Project, subject to the legal homologation process stipulated in Article 3 of Ministerial
Decree No. 047/CAB/MIN/EDD/AAN/MMUOS/2018 dated May 9, 2018.

2.1.17 Project Activities and Theory of Change (VCS, 3.6; CCB, G1.8)
The Project aims to implement various activities within the concession by helping communities shift
towards activities that reconcile natural resource and forest protection with economic viability, thereby
promoting a win-win system. At the same time, previously exploited areas of the concession will be set
aside for conservation purposes to ensure their preservation.

Page 14
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
14
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
The Project will target all populations living within the concession. The project therefore plans to support
community activities in the 63 villages identified in the concession, ensuring that inclusive and
representative actions are promoted, with a particular focus on women and vulnerable peoples.
The project is based on eight main areas of action:
- Component A: Establishment of a governance framework ;
- Component B: Institutional support ;
- Component C: Implementation of planned investments, as identified in the strategic
management plans ;
- Component D: Other investments in LDCs (Local Development Committees) ;
- Component E: Development of value chains based on perennial crops ;
- Component F: Investments in infrastructure (roads, bridges) of common interest to restore
connectivity between territories ;
- Component G: Support for the most vulnerable communities ;
- Component H: Support for family planning.
Component A: Establishment of a governance framework.
The formation of Local Development Committees (LDCs) at the village level is essential to the success of
the Lisala REDD+ Project. The Agriculture Act (December 2011), supplemented by an enabling act
published in December 2013, describes how all villages located within concessions can be organized
into LDCs. Each LDC can represent groups of two to four villages whose territory is under the authority of
the same traditional leader (land chief). These LDCs will form councils for agriculture and rural
management (CARGs) for each sector and zone (sectoral and zonal CARGs), and it is planned that they
will use mapping tools for natural resource and land management.
The basic methodology of the Lisala REDD+ Project is to strengthen the organizational structure of
territorial areas and Decentralized Territorial Entities (DTEs) based on the model of local development
committees (LDCs) and agriculture and rural management councils (CARGs) recommended by the
Ministry of Rural Development. This strengthening will be achieved through the creation or regeneration
of these institutions and their eventual official legal recognition. Traditional political structures, such as
the elected members of future DTEs, will work closely with these institutions. The training of the CLDs
will be organized and delivered by the Congolese NGO AMAR, which will be responsible for informing and
encouraging communities to join the LDCs and then supporting the creation of these LDCs in each
territory.
These institutions will be responsible for formulating Natural Resource Management Plans (NRMPs) for
village territories. These plans, which will be launched at the level of cultivated village territories up to
sectors (DTEs), groupings (based on customary organization) and LDCs, will lead to a collective analysis
of the evolution of natural resources and the factors of deforestation and forest degradation. They will

Page 15
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
15
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
result in the planning of appropriate measures to ensure that this evolution is sustainable over time while
improving the living conditions of the populations.
The methodology for implementing the Natural Resource Management Plans (NRMPs) includes:
(i) The delimitation of the main types of vegetation cover using satellite images, validated in a
participatory manner;
(ii) Inventory of land use and tenure patterns;
(iii) Creation of a mapped inventory of biodiversity and associated threats;
(iv) Estimation of local communities' agricultural land needs and identification of expansion
areas;
(v) Participatory definition of actions to be taken in the areas concerned (savannah, forests, non-
timber forest products, fisheries, flooded forests, infrastructure).
These elements will be developed in a participatory manner to ensure that qualified representatives of
all relevant groups participate in program meetings and that their specific interests are understood and
addressed separately and specifically in the program. This includes women, youth and vulnerable groups.
The program will take into account ongoing initiatives on georeferenced village lands, including the
Rainforest Foundation UK's “Mapping for Rights” project.
To achieve these results, it will be necessary to:
a. Establish Councils for Agriculture and Rural Management (CARGs);
b. Engage Local Implementing Agencies (LIAs), which will be local NGOs, to establish (or re-
establish) and georeference the boundaries of village cultivated plots;
c. Train and equip these LMAs;
d. Create Local Development Committees (LDCs), demarcate their plots and register them;
e. Verify the socio-environmental compliance of these plans and conduct the necessary socio-
environmental studies;
f. Monitor and evaluate implementation.
Benefits for the community:
Strengthening community structures will reinforce community organization and promote inclusive
representation in institutions and the project. These LDCs will also enable communities to create
a forum for discussion on the development of their land. This will strengthen the representation
of vulnerable groups and reduce discrimination and inequality.
Climate and biodiversity:

Page 16
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
16
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
The development of NRMPs will ensure the sustainable and efficient use of resources, enabling
the protection and restoration of forest ecosystems and biodiversity by reducing pressure on their
resources.
In the long term, these measures will promote carbon storage and climate change mitigation.
Component B: Institutional support.
Decentralized government services need effective organization and adequate resources to fulfill their
mission. The validation of management plans and, above all, the smooth implementation of agreements
between LDCs are essential to improve the coordination and effectiveness of the teams from the three
ministries responsible for village territories (agriculture, environment/forests, rural development).
To implement this component, the Project plans to:
a. Support the drafting and promulgation of regulations relating to the Agricultural Law of
December 24, 2011, which provides for the creation of land advisory councils and their territorial
entities at the primary level, implement the draft law recognizing CARG areas, support local
development committees (LDCs), organize their functioning and provide support for the
implementation of legal provisions relating to the creation and implementation (by the Ministry
of Rural Development) of CARGs and LDCs ;
b. Align existing structures with the new regulations, for example by adopting recommendations
based on the new law and providing training on the new responsibilities and functions arising
from the law, particularly in the land sector ;
c. The Ministry of Environment needs assistance to improve its capacity to supervise forest
management activities. Units within the Ministry of Rural Development and the provincial Ministry
of Agriculture need to be able to register the status of relevant organizations (i.e., LDCs) and
provide relevant registration documents to interested parties ;
d. Establish a complaint and appeal mechanism, either by facilitating access to the courts or by
improving the supervision of employees by their superiors ;
e. Strengthen decentralized services through training and the provision of equipment ;
f. Facilitate field missions in villages.
Benefits for the community:
Component B will strengthen public institutions, particularly in the agricultural sector. This strengthening
will help preserve the long-term benefits of the project.
Climate and biodiversity:
The creation of LDCs promotes a local and sustainable governance framework for resource management.
Component C: Implementation of planned investments, as identified in the strategic management plans.

Page 17
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
17
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
This component will be implemented through various means, including:
(i) various forms of training (initial training, field schools, etc.);
(ii) initial investment and provision of inputs;
(iii) payment for results or Payment for Environmental Services (PES).
Investments will target traditional smallholders who can benefit from the project on areas ranging from
5 to 20 hectares for plantations and 50 to 100 hectares for protected areas. These farmers must have
secured land rights and their land must be located in areas approved by the LDCs.
Various investments will be possible, including the development of agriculture in savannah areas
(plantations, agroforestry, firebreaks), improving the sustainability of agroforestry, and protecting
biodiversity-rich forests.
Benefits for communities:
Component C will promote community economic development by strengthening agricultural activities and
infrastructure. These investments aim to improve the quality of life in villages and reduce poverty.
Climate and biodiversity:
Some of the planned activities have significant environmental benefits, including the development of
agroforestry and the protection of savannahs against fires. These actions will promote the return of
biodiversity to areas severely degraded by fire. They will also reduce pressure on forests by developing
agricultural activities in the savannah.
Component D: Other investments in LDCs
LDCs can receive support in various areas such as co-management of fisheries, creation of fish ponds,
and small-scale processing equipment.
Climate and biodiversity:
Component D supports sustainable fishing practices and rational management of fish stocks. Fish stocks
are now seriously threatened by population growth, which is putting severe pressure on stock renewal.
Benefits for communities:
NGOs will provide support for the development of sustainable fishing activities.
Component E: Development of value chains from perennial crops.
The objective of this component is to strengthen or revitalize value chains for local products, particularly
rubber, palm oil, coffee, and cocoa. This includes support and assistance to producers to improve the
value of their products, to facilitate the purchase of equipment, to support local processing centers, to
promote trade routes, to develop fair trade certification. To achieve these objectives, the project will sign
agreements with downstream operators in the sector. These agreements will aim at identifying
professional operators working at fair prices. These operators are: (i) cooperatives or producer

Page 18
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
18
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
associations, such as the one operating in the cocoa sector (see below); (ii) large private operators
already present in the region (forest concessionaires or livestock farmers) who wish to diversify their
activities ; or (iii) private companies already established in the DRC and wishing to invest in the provinces
of Mongala. The Project provides the necessary resources to identify these operators and co-finance their
establishment in the region.
Benefits for the community:
The revitalization of the agricultural sectors and value chains will enable sustainable agricultural
economic development for the populations.
Climate and biodiversity:
The development of more sustainable agricultural chains reduces pressure on resources and forests.
Component F: Investments in infrastructure of common interest to restore connectivity between
territories.
Despite its extensive river network and the significant progress made since 2010 in terms of commercial
vessel profitability and substantial investment in this area, entire provinces remain isolated because river
boats remain a dangerous and slow means of transport, and trucks have difficulty accessing the province
of Mongala. The following priorities have been identified in the area of transport:
• Stricter regulation of river passenger transport and the equipment of these boats (spare
engines, night lighting), as well as load control;
• Completion and maintenance of commercial roads within concessions, including the
reconstruction of wooden bridges where necessary;
• Maintenance of the most important rural tracks leading to waterways and connecting the main
towns in the Lisala territory.
Benefits for communities:
The economic development of villages is severely hampered by their isolation. Restoring communication
links would promote strong economic development and improve access to healthcare and education.
Component G: Support for the most vulnerable communities.
The Project fully integrates vulnerable groups into local project governance to avoid discrimination and
encourages their participation in activities.
Benefits for the communities:
This component aims to support the most vulnerable communities while avoiding any negative impact
on their way of life and traditions.
Component H: Support for family planning

Page 19
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
19
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
The Project supports the permanent recruitment of local NGOs (one per territory) to promote, in close
collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the following activities among the 12,000 farming households
in the concession:
• Information/awareness-raising on family planning methods with the support of opinion leaders
(political, traditional and religious), combined with access to contraceptive methods. These family
planning methods will also be extended to the prevention of Ebola and HIV/AIDS;
• Education for young people, particularly girls, to promote access to employment and the setting
of reasonable targets for the number of children per family.
Benefits for the community:
This aspect aims to reduce poverty and improve the health of populations through awareness and
prevention.
Climate and biodiversity:
Awareness of family planning aims to prevent excessive population growth, which would increase
pressure on forests.

2.1.18 Sustainable Development Contributions (VCS, 3.17)
The DRC is committed to sustainable development within the framework of the 2030 Agenda for
Sustainable Development and has adapted the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) established at
the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20 Conference). This 2030 Agenda
comprises 17 global goals with 169 targets, measured using 232 specific indicators, which address the
social, economic and environmental dimensions of sustainable development. In 2016, the DRC
established the Congolese Observatory for Sustainable Development, a framework that monitors,
evaluates and reports on the implementation of the SDGs. The DRC's strategy is based on an approach
that integrates stakeholder awareness and the implementation of public policies with a strong focus on
SDGs that incorporate the social dimension. The country also prioritizes the environmental dimension
with a commitment to preserving its natural resources. The Lisala REDD+ Project aims to contribute to
these national priorities by promoting the achievement of SDGs that incorporate social and environmental
dimensions.
All SDGs integrated into the project are listed in the table below.

particularly prevalent in isolated areas of
the DRC where food supplies are

2.2 Without-project Land Use Scenario and Additionality
2.2.1 Conditions Prior to Project Initiation and Land Use Scenarios without the Project
(VCS, 3.13; CCB, G2.1)
The Lisala REDD+ Project was not implemented with the intent of artificially generating greenhouse gas
(GHG) emissions for the purpose of their subsequent reduction, removal, or destruction. All historical and
ongoing deforestation observed within the project area results from prevailing socio-economic drivers,
demographic pressures, and governance challenges, entirely independent of any project planning activities.
The project area is located within the Congo Basin rainforest ecosystem, characterized by dense tropical
moist broadleaf forests with high levels of biodiversity and significant carbon storage capacity. This
ecosystem is globally recognized as a critical biodiversity hotspot and plays a vital role in both regional and
global climate regulation.
Historically, the Lisala concession was predominantly covered by intact and semi-intact tropical forests,
utilized intermittently by local communities for subsistence activities such as hunting, gathering, and small-
scale shifting agriculture. In past decades, the area was formally allocated as a commercial logging
concession and underwent industrial-scale timber harvesting under regulated forestry operations.
However, even during its tenure as a logging concession, the area faced increasing pressure from
unplanned deforestation and forest degradation driven by local community activities. These pressures —
notably slash-and-burn agriculture, charcoal production, and informal fuelwood extraction — have
intensified in recent years, fueled by population growth and limited alternative livelihoods. Recognizing

Page 33
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
33
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
these growing threats, the concession was acquired and converted into a conservation concession to focus
on reducing deforestation dynamics through collaborative efforts with local communities.
Environmental conditions prior to project initiation reflect both the ecological richness of the region and the
cumulative impacts of human activities. The area experiences a tropical humid climate with bimodal rainfall
patterns, receiving an average of approximately 1,800 mm of rainfall annually, and mean annual
temperatures ranging between 23.9°C and 25.4°C (Fick, S.E. and Hijmans, R.J., 2017. WorldClim 2: new
1 km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology, 37(12):
4302-4315). Hydrologically, the landscape is interlaced with numerous small rivers and tributaries of the
Congo River, resulting in seasonal flooding across some lowland zones. The terrain is moderately
undulating, with elevations ranging from 300 to 500 meters above sea level, and an average elevation of
approximately 400 meters (Copernicus DEM, ESA/European Commission, 2020). Soils are predominantly
classified as Ferralsols (FRx) and Gleysols (Gle), typical of humid tropical forests, characterized by low
fertility and high acidity, suitable only for short-term cultivation following forest clearing (Batjes NH 2007.
SOTER-based soil parameter estimates for Central Africa - DR of Congo, Burundi and Rwanda(SOTWIScaf,
version 1.0). Report 2007/02, ISRIC - World Soil Information, Wageningen). Vegetation within the project
area comprises largely closed-canopy primary forest, while the surrounding landscapes include
settlements, subsistence agriculture, and areas of secondary vegetation.
In the absence of the Lisala REDD+ Project, unplanned deforestation and forest degradation would be
expected to continue across the concession. The primary drivers of deforestation would remain the
expansion of slash-and-burn agriculture, driven by population growth and land scarcity; increasing charcoal
production to meet regional energy demands; informal timber extraction for local use and informal trade;
and infrastructure development occurring without integrated land-use planning. Without intervention, these
dynamics would be expected to lead to progressive forest loss, fragmentation resulting in significant
reductions in carbon stocks and posing severe threats to local biodiversity. These baseline dynamics have
been modeled and quantified in the baseline scenario, reflecting the continuation of the trends and
conditions prevailing prior to project initiation.
As the baseline scenario is consistent with the ongoing land-use dynamics existing prior to the start of the
project, further details are provided in Section 3.1.4.

2.5 Legal Status and Property Rights
2.5.1 National and Local Laws (VCS, 3.1, 3.6. 3.7, 3.14, 3.18, 3.19; CCB, G5.6)
The DRC has been committed to and has supported the REDD+ process since 2008, as evidenced by its
early selection in the Forest Investment Program (FIP). The FIP is part of the national REDD+ process and
serves as the primary source of funding to enable the country to enter an investment phase, undertake
the large-scale operational deployment of REDD+, and launch the first sectoral transformation program
in 2015. In 2012, the government adopted a national REDD+ strategy (CAFI,20123), which outlines how
it can meet its long-term development aspirations through a green economy. This strategy aims to
stabilize forest cover across two-thirds of the country’s area by 2030 and maintain it thereafter. More
recently, the government has developed a large-scale REDD+ program for results-based payments in the
3 « Stratégie-cadre Nationale REDD+_RDC_Résumé pr Décideurs_2012.pdf ».

Page 38
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
38
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
Mai-Ndombe province, with the goal of having a significant impact on the climate and delivering crucial
development benefits, while generating unprecedented learning for the FCPF Carbon Fund.
The project is aligned with the ambitious goals of the FIP and draws inspiration from the actions
implemented in Mai-Ndombe aimed at establishing a green development program.
Throughout the project period, Taranis Operations Limited (Project Proponent), Taranis Congo
(concession owner) and The Shared Wood Company Kongo (Project Operator) will ensure that the project
and an all the activities are carried out in accordance with national and international regulations. The
Lisala REDD+ Project complies with all applicable local, district, and national laws, regulations, and
standards. Within the project area, none of the proposed project activities violates any law.

excluded from height
requirement.
Land in the project area has qualified as forest
for at least the 10 years (i.e. before 2014) prior
to the project start date (2025), as confirmed
by the Joint Research Centre (JRC) Tropical

VM0007 [2]
Where land within the project
area is peatland or tidal
wetlands and emissions from
the SOC pool are deemed
significant, the relevant WRC
modules are applied
alongside other relevant
modules
Peatlands have been identified in portions of
the project area using peat thickness and
extent data provided by Crezee et al. (2022). In
accordance with VM0007 requirements, a
significance assessment of potential Soil
Organic Carbon (SOC) emissions from these
peat areas has been conducted using the test
described in Annex 1 of VM0007. The results
demonstrated that the anticipated SOC
emissions are deemed not significant (de
minimis). As a result, the Wetlands Restoration
and Conservation (WRC) modules are not
applied
VM0007 [3]
Baseline deforestation is
unplanned (AUDef) or planned
(APDef).
The baseline deforestation is unplanned
(AUDef), primarily driven by shifting agriculture,
charcoal production, and fuelwood collection.
VM0007 [4]
Flooding agricultural lands or
intensifying livestock
production via feed-lots or
manure lagoons for leakage
prevention is not allowed.
Project activities do not involve flooding
agricultural lands or livestock intensification.
Proposed land uses include agroforestry and
low-intensity subsistence agriculture.
VM0007 [5]
Baseline agents of
deforestation: clear land for
tree harvesting or small-scale
ag., lack legal right to
deforest, and are residents or
immigrants.
Baseline agents are local households
practicing slash-and-burn agriculture without
formal land tenure.
VM0007 [6] Post-deforestation land use is
reforestation
Not applicable. The baseline post-deforestation
land use is agricultural expansion, not
reforestation.
VT0001 [1]
AFOLU activities same or
similar to the proposed
activity must not violate any
applicable law, even if not
enforced.
All AFOLU activities implemented in the project
comply with national and provincial laws of the
Democratic Republic of Congo, including
forestry, land tenure, and environmental
regulations. Legal compliance has been
assessed and documented in the legal
compliance section.

VMD0001 [1]
This module is applicable to
all forest types and age
classes.
The module is applicable as the project area
comprises tropical moist forests.
VMD0007 [1]
Applicable for estimating
baseline emissions from
unplanned deforestation in
forest land converting to non-
forest land. Landscape can be
mosaic, transition, or frontier.
The module applies as the project baseline
includes unplanned deforestation with patterns
matching transition configurations, as
evidenced by historical spatial analysis of
deforestation.
VMD0007 [2]
Baseline agents: (i) clear land
for settlements, agriculture,
ranching or aquaculture (not
large-scale); (ii) lack legal
right to deforest; (iii) are
residents or immigrants in the
reference region.
Baseline deforestation agents in the reference
region are primarily smallholder farmers and
charcoal producers. They operate without legal
rights to clear land and are either local
residents or migrants.
VMD0010 [1]
Applicable for estimating
carbon stock changes and
GHG emissions from
displaced activities causing
deforestation or wetland
degradation outside the
project area.
The project applies this module to estimate
carbon stock changes and GHG emissions from
potential displacement of deforestation
activities outside the project area.
VMD0010 [2]
Activities subject to
displacement include
conversion of forest land to
grazing/cropland/other land
uses, or conversion of
intact/partially degraded
wetlands to
drained/degraded wetlands.
Potential displaced activities include primarily
the conversion of forest land to cropland,
driven by local agricultural expansion
pressures.
VMD0010 [3]
Mandatory if module BL-UP is
used to define the baseline ;
full compliance with BL-UP
applicability conditions
required.
Module BL-UP is used in this project. All
associated applicability conditions are met.
VMD0013 [1]
Applicable to REDD project
activities with emissions from
biomass burning.
Biomass burning could occur in the baseline
due to slash-and-burn agriculture and
occasional uncontrolled fires. Inclusion of fire
emissions in the baseline is optional under this
module. The project is evaluating whether to
include these emissions in baseline accounting
or conservatively exclude them.
VMD0015 [1]
Strata as defined in baseline
modules are fixed and may
not be changed without
baseline revision.
Baseline strata differentiating mineral soils
and peatlands have been established during
initial project design under the REDD+ MF
methodology. No changes will occur unless a

Page 50
CCB & VCS Project Description Template
CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4
50
CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4
formal baseline revision is undertaken.
VMD0015 [2] Requirements for logging
activities
Not applicable. No logging activities are
planned within the project boundary.
VMD0016 [1]
Module must be used to
delineate peat vs non-peat
and stratify peat by depth and
emission characteristics
unless SOC emissions are de
minimis.
Peat vs. non-peat zones have been delineated
using peat thickness and extent data from
Crezee et al. (2022). An assessment of the
significance of SOC emissions was conducted
following the test described in Annex 1 of
VM0007, which determined that anticipated
SOC emissions are de minimis in the context of
the methodology.
VMD0017 [1]
Mandatory module when
using REDD+ MF
methodology, applicable for
estimating uncertainty in
emissions/removals from
REDD and WRC activities.
The project uses the REDD+ MF methodology,
therefore application of VMD0017 is
mandatory. The project complies with this
requirement.
VMD0017 [2]
Covers uncertainties in
deforestation/degradation
rates, carbon pool stock
estimates and changes, peat
emissions, and project
emissions.
The project’s uncertainty assessment includes
deforestation rates, carbon stock estimates,
and project emissions, ensuring that all
parameters required by the module are
covered.
VMD0017 [3]
If uncertainty value is
unknown or not easily
calculable, a justified
conservative estimate can be
used, including 0% if
indisputable.
Where field data is not available, the project
uses conservative estimates based on peer-
reviewed literature and IPCC defaults.
VMD0017 [4]
A 95% confidence interval
with a half-width ≤ 15% of the
recorded value must be
targeted, particularly for
carbon stock measurements.
The sampling design for forest carbon stocks
inventory and estimation targets a 95%
confidence level and ≤15% relative precision.
Random sampling, sample size optimization,
and QA/QC procedures support this objective,
in accordance with REDD+ MF requirements.
